name: Today's Report
headline: Repeat buyers made 78% of U.S. home purchases; here, the typical first-time down payment on the five city median is about $90,000.
teaser: Repeat buyers made 78% of U.S. home purchases, wholesale prices rose 6.5% from a year ago with home building materials up 9.8%, chip stocks fell before Nvidia's earnings, and our Bay East board eased to 2,408 listings.

rates.source: Mortgage News Daily, the latest for November 16, updated 9:15 AM PT. This report was written before that update, at 7.50% and 7.03%

sections.label: Real estate
sections.html:
Repeat buyers own this market. Repeat buyers made 78% of U.S. home purchases in the year to June, according to the National Association of REALTORS® 2026 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers. Their median age is 62 and first-time buyers' is 40, both tying records; the typical buyer overall is 58, and the first-time share edged up to 22% from a record low 21%.

Here, the gap is the down payment. NAR's median first-time buyer put down 9% and the median repeat buyer 19%. On our five city median list price of $999,988, that is about $90,000 down and $6,363 a month for a first-time buyer, against $190,000 down and $5,664 for a repeat buyer, at Mortgage News Daily's 7.50% from Friday, before taxes and insurance. Equity from the last house is doing a lot of the lifting.

What it means for you. If you are buying your first home, 9% down is the national norm, so get preapproved on what you have rather than waiting for 20%. If you are selling, most of today's buyers arrive with equity, and a well priced home still draws them even at 7.50%.

Today's count. Board wide: 2,408 listings across the 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, down from 2,421 Sunday, with 134 coming soon and 144 brand new. The five city ledger carries 606 live listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City, 539 on the market and 67 coming soon, down from 616.

Fremont holds 205 live listings: 164 active, 26 coming soon and 15 brand new, with a median on market list price of $1,249,990 at $783 a square foot and a typical listing out 38 days; with 20% down at 7.50%, that median runs about $6,992 a month in principal and interest. Hayward carries 175, Milpitas 98, Newark 71 and Union City 57. Across all five cities the median is $999,988 at $666 a square foot, 271 homes are priced under a million, and 188 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

images.alt: Donut chart: repeat buyers made 78% of U.S. home purchases from July 2025 to June 2026 (median age 62, 19% median down payment) and first-time buyers 22% (median age 40, 9% down). Local panel: on the five city median list price of $999,988, 9% down is $90,000 and $6,363 a month in principal and interest at 7.50%; 19% down is $190,000 and $5,664 a month.
images.caption: Repeat buyers dominate, and their bigger down payments cut the monthly cost by about $700 on our median home.

sections.label: Economy
sections.html:
Wholesale prices are near a four year high. Producer prices rose 0.3% in October and 6.5% from a year earlier, the fastest pace since November 2022. What builders pay for the materials in a new home rose 9.8%, also the fastest since November 2022, and that cost lands in the price of new construction.

Rates and metals. With consumer prices up 0.4% in October as well, a December rate increase stays on the table. The 10-Year Treasury yield is near 5.13%, against Friday's 5.15% close. Gold is near $3,861.30, down 0.64% from Friday's settlement, silver has dropped 5.11% to $46.61, and Brent is down about 2.5% this morning; the Brent figure above is Friday's settlement.

images.alt: Line chart, Producer Price Index change from a year earlier, not seasonally adjusted, October 2025 to October 2026: final demand rose from 2.8% to 6.5% and inputs to residential construction from 2.8% to 9.8%, both the fastest since November 2022.
images.caption: Wholesale prices are up 6.5% from a year ago, and home building materials 9.8%.

sections.label: Stocks
sections.html:
Chips led a Monday slide. As of 8:15 AM PT the S&P 500 was down 1.22%, the Nasdaq 1.81% and the Dow 0.65%, with the Philadelphia semiconductor index off 4.44%. Fremont's Lam Research was down 5.21% and Milpitas's KLA 4.20%.

A big week for Bay Area tickers. Nvidia, down 2.57% at $158.66, reports Tuesday after the close, its first report since Jensen Huang stepped down as chief executive. Market Briefs also expects Anthropic, the San Francisco company behind Claude, to go public this week; its filing offers 825 million shares at $70 to $78, up to about $64.4 billion. The numbers above are live, not closes.

sections.label: Crypto
sections.html: Bitcoin touched a four month low this weekend. It slid to about $62,600 Saturday evening, its lowest since mid July, and is near $64,220, down 0.61% over the past 24 hours, live from CoinGecko at 8:15 AM PT. Ether is near $1,812.61 and XRP near $0.95. With the 10-Year Treasury above 5%, a safer yield is competing for the same money.
